title: How a smartwatch counts your steps
examples: How does my watch count steps?
Why does my watch count steps in the car?

explain.say: Inside a smartwatch is an accelerometer, a chip with a tiny silicon weight on springs. When your arm speeds up or slows down, the weight shifts slightly, and the chip measures that shift as acceleration.

draw.text: How a smartwatch counts your steps

explain.say: When you walk, your body bobs up and down and your arm swings, so the acceleration rises and falls in a regular wave. Each peak, as your foot strikes the ground, is a likely step.
Software smooths the signal and counts only peaks that are big enough and come in a steady rhythm, roughly one to three a second. That way a single wave of your hand is not counted as walking.
Some watches also use a gyroscope and your stride length to estimate distance. Counts are usually close when walking, but pushing a pram, where your wrist stays still, can fool them.

faq.a: An accelerometer measures changes in speed and direction. The one in a watch is a tiny silicon structure with a movable weight on springs; when the watch accelerates, the weight lags behind, and the chip measures how far it moved.

faq.q: How does a smartwatch tell a step from waving my arm?
faq.a: Walking makes a repeating pattern of peaks at a steady pace. The software looks for several similar peaks in a row at a walking rhythm, and ignores single jolts or random movements.
asks: Why doesn't clapping count as steps?

faq.q: Why does my watch count steps when I'm in a car?
faq.a: A bumpy road can shake your wrist in a rhythm that looks like walking. Watches try to filter this out, but steady bumps can sometimes fool the step-counting software.
asks: Why did my watch count steps when I wasn't walking?

faq.a: For normal walking, wrist step counters are usually within a few percent of the real count. They are less accurate when your arm is still, such as holding a trolley or rail.

faq.q: How does a watch know distance walked?
faq.a: It multiplies your steps by an estimated stride length worked out from your height, or it uses GPS outdoors to measure the distance directly.
asks: How does a fitness tracker measure distance?

facts: MEMS accelerometers detect the movement of a tiny silicon proof mass by measuring changes in capacitance.
The popular 10,000 steps a day goal traces back to a 1965 Japanese pedometer called manpo-kei, meaning 10,000 steps meter.
